title: Full Of and Without
kidRule: The ending FUL means 'full of', but it has only one L: powerful. The ending LESS means 'without', and it keeps both S's: harmless.
hint: This word is a small word with an ending stuck on. Spell the small word first, then think carefully about how many letters the ending needs.
reminder: The ending F-U-L has just one L, and the ending L-E-S-S has two S's.

check.question: Why does POWERFUL have only one L at the end?
check.correctAnswer: When FUL is an ending that means 'full of', it always has just one L!
distractors: Because long words are never allowed a double letter
Because the second L is there but it stays quiet

words.sent: A powerful wind blew my hat away.
words.story: Ants are very powerful for their size: some can carry things many times heavier than their own bodies!
words.card: The *powerful* ant used all its *power* to carry a whole cupcake!

words.sent: The little garden snake is harmless.
words.story: The harmless hoverfly wears yellow and black stripes that make it look like a wasp, so hungry birds leave it alone!
words.card: The *harmless* octopus gave me a hug with every *arm*!

words.def: Perfectly clean, with not even one mark.
words.sent: We scrubbed the kitchen floor until it was spotless.
words.story: Cats spend a big part of their waking day licking their fur to keep it spotless!
words.card: The *spotless* *pot* was so clean that the frog used it as a mirror!

words.sent: The colorful parrot squawked at us.
words.story: The rainbow lorikeet is a colorful parrot with blue, green, orange, and yellow feathers all on one bird!
words.card: Red *or* blue? The *colorful* chameleon could not decide!

words.sent: The fearless firefighter climbed the tall ladder.
words.story: The honey badger is often called the most fearless animal in the world, because it will even stand up to lions!
words.card: The *fearless* mouse whispered a joke in the lion's *ear*!

words.def: Kind, and careful to think about what other people need.
words.sent: It was thoughtful of you to save me a seat.
words.story: People around the world celebrate World Kindness Day every year on November 13, a day for thoughtful acts like sharing and helping!
words.card: You *ought* to be *thoughtful* and share your pickles with the penguin!

words.def: Not able to stay still or calm.
words.sent: The restless kids wiggled in their seats.
words.story: Some sharks have to keep swimming all the time to breathe, so they look restless day and night!
words.card: The *restless* sloth just could not *rest*, so he ran a marathon!

words.def: So good that it fills you with delight.
words.sent: We had a wonderful day at the beach.
words.story: Long ago, people made a list of seven wonderful sights called the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, and only the Great Pyramid of Giza is still standing!
words.card: I *won* a *wonderful* wobbly jelly at the fair!

words.def: So surprised that you cannot think of anything to say.
words.sent: The surprise party left Grandpa speechless.
words.story: Giraffes were once thought to be almost speechless, but scientists have recorded them humming to each other at night!
words.card: The parrot gave a long *speech* that left the pirate *speechless*!

words.def: Doing well at what you set out to do.
words.sent: Our bake sale was successful and every cookie was sold.
words.story: The Wright brothers made their first successful airplane flight in 1903, and it lasted only 12 seconds!
words.card: The secret of *success* is a *successful* nap, said the sloth!
